name: heldout
note: Out-of-distribution: SAME 10 lints, DIFFERENT code. The riir-clippy corpus does NOT contain these fixes — only a same-lint template. This is the generalization axis; the seed set only measures retrieval. Fixes chosen to have a single canonical idiomatic form so normalized exact-match stays a fair grader for both arms.

cases.buggy: fn bar(x: i32) -> i32 { return x + 1; }

fn sq(x: u32) -> u32 { x * x }
fn run(v: Vec<u32>) -> Vec<u32> { v.into_iter().map(|n| sq(n)).collect() }
cases.want:
fn sq(x: u32) -> u32 { x * x }
fn run(v: Vec<u32>) -> Vec<u32> { v.into_iter().map(sq).collect() }

cases.buggy:
fn count(v: &Vec<u8>) -> usize { v.len() }
fn go(mut v: Vec<u8>) -> usize { count(&mut v) }
cases.want:
fn count(v: &Vec<u8>) -> usize { v.len() }
fn go(v: Vec<u8>) -> usize { count(&v) }

cases.buggy:
fn show(s: &str) -> usize { s.len() }
